hero.caption: Original Caption: Technicians at the U.S. Air Force guided missile test base at Holloman Air Force Base, Alamogordo, New Mexico, rig the rocket launcher to a JB-2 buzz bomb just before a test flight of the pulse-jet subsonic missile. A copy of the Nazi V-1 which rained down on London during the war, this missile still yields important data in tests conducted by Air Force research engineers.

images.filename: USS Carbonero (SS-337) launching Loon missile in 1949.jpg
images.caption: The U.S. Navy submarine USS Carbonero (SS-337) launching a JB-2 Loon missile off Hawaii (USA). Two Loons were launched by Carbonero and USS Cusk (SSG-348), equipped with smoke generators, to fly as aerial targets over ships of the U.S. First Task Fleet, centered around the aircraft carriers USS Boxer (CV-21) and USS Valley Forge (CV-45). However, the jet-propelled targets could not be shot down by either anti-aircraft artillery or fighter planes during its flight of 130 km.
images.alt: The U.S. Navy submarine USS Carbonero (SS-337) launching a JB-2 Loon missile off Hawaii (USA).
